newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline remains firm late after API rally.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline remains firm late after API rally.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline remained firm Wednesday afternoon amid conflicting oil inventory data which showed a bullish gasoline stock draw but yielded suspect implied demand, dealers said.
"We went up on the APIs, but the numbers weren't really believable, so the market started to look shaky, and then nobody wanted to sell, so we are all holding tight," said a New York gasoline dealer.
At 1404 EDT, June gasoline was up 0.79 cent at 61.10 cents a gallon. June heating oil was off 0.03 cent at 53.50 cents a gallon while June crude was up nine cents a barrel at $19.75.

"We ran up early and loaded up on length, but there has been very little follow through, so I think we are going to close around unchanged," said a New York crude dealer, noting light late session profit-taking may occur when the market is convinced the session's highs have already been made.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) said Tuesday evening that gasoline stocks dropped 3.6 million barrels for the week ended May 2. Dealers had been expecting the API to report a build of one to two million barrels.
The draw widened the year-over-year gasoline stock deficit to 13.2 million barrels.

But, the stock data yielded an implied demand figure for gasoline of 8.7 million barrels per day (bpd) which dealers said was an all-time record. The implied demand made dealers skeptical of the data since they said it is still too early in the driving season to get such high demand.
Dealers also pointed out that cash gasoline values would have been much higher in the New York Harbor and U.S. Gulf last week if demand was as high during that period as the API data suggested.
